claims.claim: The fine mesh of mosquito bed-nets (usually 3 mm or less), designed to exclude mosquitoes, makes them almost entirely unselective fishing gear that captures small fish.
claims.episode_span: A few fisheries researchers noted that the polyethylene netting was stronger and finer than traditional papyrus or sisal gear
claims.source_title: Mosquito net use in artisanal East African fisheries (Short et al. 2018) - PLOS ONE
claims.supporting_quote: Fine mesh sizes (usually ≤3mm) are critical for exclusion of mosquitos, but render MNs used in fisheries almost entirely unselective in terms of small fish.

claims.claim: GiveWell estimates that insecticide-treated net campaigns cost approximately $3,000 to $8,000 per death averted.
claims.episode_span: a few dollars per net delivered, and on careful modern estimates a few thousand dollars per life saved
claims.source_title: Mass Distribution of Insecticide-Treated Nets (ITNs) | GiveWell
claims.supporting_quote: We estimate that it costs approximately $3,000 to $8,000 to avert a death in locations where GiveWell supports campaigns.

claims.claim: Randomized trials found insecticide-treated nets reduce all-cause child mortality, saving about 5.6 lives per year for every 1,000 children protected.
claims.episode_span: randomized trials showed they could cut child mortality from malaria by roughly 15 to 20 percent in areas of stable transmission
claims.source_title: Insecticide-treated nets for preventing malaria - Cochrane
claims.supporting_quote: we concluded that ITNs reduce the child mortality from all causes, corresponding to a saving of 5.6 lives each year for every 1000 children protected with ITNs

claims.claim: Mosquito nets used for fishing retain almost all fish, including immature and small fish, causing harmful ecological consequences.
claims.episode_span: Because the mesh was designed to stop mosquitoes, it also captured fingerlings and small cichlids that traditional nets had allowed to escape.
claims.supporting_quote: When used for fishing, mosquito nets have harmful ecological consequences because the fine mesh of a mosquito net retains almost all fish, including bycatch such as immature or small fish and fish species that are not suitable for consumption.

claims.claim: Most distributed mosquito nets are treated with insecticides, commonly permethrin, which is water soluble — raising contamination concerns when nets are used in water.
claims.episode_span: Insecticide residues washed into the lake during repeated use, adding low-level chemical pressure to an already stressed aquatic system.
claims.source_title: Mosquito net use in artisanal East African fisheries (Short et al. 2018) - PLOS ONE
claims.supporting_quote: the majority of these MNs are treated with insecticides, commonly Permethrin which is water soluble

claims.claim: Mosquito nets have been distributed at enormous scale — at least 154 million in 2015 alone, with similar numbers in previous years.
claims.episode_span: Between 2004 and 2015, more than one billion long-lasting insecticidal nets were distributed across Africa
claims.source_title: Mosquito net use in artisanal East African fisheries (Short et al. 2018) - PLOS ONE
claims.supporting_quote: With at least 154 million MNs estimated to have been distributed in 2015, and similar numbers in previous years
